chapter: Blanton, Los Angeles and Art Tatum
title: What Blanton was like as a person; egotism among musicians
summary: Blanton was pleasant company though perhaps fast-living; Stewart says few musicians were egotistical.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now, did you -- what kind of a guy was he?
Oh, he was very pleasant, wonderful person.
Was he -- was he a fast living guy? Did he --
I think it was a bit fast living, you know, because, you know, I didn't see very much of him.
Because you were working a lot too.
Yeah, I would be working, and we'd probably pass each other by, going different directions, you know, and what little I did see of him, he was wonderful company.
So he wasn't an egotistical guy then?

I didn't run across many musicians who were egotistical, you know. There were a few, of course, you know. I don't see why it would happen like that, but they thought they were better than everybody else and what have you. That has happened.
